transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~62 mins
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Dr. Aisha Rahman (Sable Head of ML), Tom Greer (Sable Platform), Sophie Lin (Sable Security)

Summary:
Quick migration/ consolidation demo: show parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API, console tour (deploys, routing, cost/latency dashboards), and Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization. Customer wants predictability and data controls for clinical workloads.

Topics covered:
- Mapping endpoints & prompt/response parity
- Latency & cost tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- KV cache / prefix caching + batching configuration
- Console observability and rollouts (canary/A-B/fallback)
- Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC, audit logs
- Pilot next steps and benchmarks

Action items (recorded at top for visibility):
- Maya: parity spreadsheet + token cost delta
- Jordan: pricing sketch + pilot docs
- Tom: traffic profiles + prompt set
- Sophie: compliance checklist

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Park: Alright, uh, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna run through a migration strategy from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood, high-level then a bit of console, and then Optimize suggestions. Maya and Liam from my side will field the deep bits.
[00:18] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Thanks. Quick context — we run clinical triage models in prod, currently split between OpenAI and Together for chat and Anthropic for safety-sensitive rerank. Our main asks are latency under 150ms 95th for short-turn dialogs, data residency, and auditability for regs.
[00:35] Maya Singh: Got it, thanks Aisha. We'll focus on parity: same prompts, same tokens, and where there are API mismatches we show our adapter recommendations. Also we'll call out performance delta and ops choices — dedicated vs hosted vs private.
[00:50] Tom Greer: One thing — we have a 2k qps spiky tail during morning sync, so autoscale behavior is big. Also we have encryption-at-rest keys in our KMS.
[01:05] Liam Ortega: Cool, will show routing rules for burst to cloud regions and fallback to cheaper variants — that helps predictable cost w/o downtime.
[01:20] Jordan Park: Quick agenda on screen — parity mapping, console tour, an Optimize run-through on batching/quant, Q&A, then next steps. Deck and parity spreadsheet link in chat: https://redwood.ai/decks/sable-migration (note: placeholder link).
[02:05] Maya Singh: Starting parity mapping — so OpenAI chat completions map to Redwood /v1/chat/generate, Anthropic assistant-type calls map to our conversational model configs, and Together-style streaming token callbacks map to Redwood's streaming with chunked events. There are some differences in function-calling semantics though — we provide a polyfill pattern in our SDK.
[02:45] Dr. Aisha Rahman: When you say polyfill, is that something we drop into node/python and then we don't touch code? How brittle is it?
[03:00] Maya Singh: Yeah, it's a small shim. Usually <200 lines, we translate the function payloads and name conventions. For edge cases where Together uses structured responses we convert to Redwood's structured-output schema; we did that for a biomed customer last quarter. Transcript note: story names get swapped so—
[03:28] Sophie Lin: On the security front, we need to see proofs of key separation — e.g., that our KMS holds encryption keys and Redwood can't access plaintext. Also audit logs with per-request IDs.
[03:45] Jordan Park: Absolutely. We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Private and Dedicated options; for hosted we offer envelope encryption + BYOK patterns and full audit logs surfaced in Console. We'll send SOC 2 artifacts and the KMS integration guide.
[04:10] Tom Greer: Any difference in token accounting? OpenAI tokenizers sometimes differ — we already have cost math tuned to those numbers.
[04:25] Maya Singh: Great point. Tokenization variations happen; our parity spreadsheet has a tokenizer-normalization column — we run both tokenizers in the adapter and normalize counts for billing and batching thresholds. We'll include sample scripts.
[04:50] [05:00] Maya Singh: Now console — screen share — top-left is an API route view; you can pin routes to a model version for canary rollout. Right side shows token cost by route and 95th latency. You mentioned 150ms 95th — we have SLOs you can set per-route and alerting hooks.
[05:30] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Can we set different SLOs for sync triage vs long-form summarization?
[05:45] Liam Ortega: Yes. The route config accepts latency SLO and a fallback policy — e.g., if 95th exceeds 200ms, route to a lower-capacity instance or different model. We also show estimated unit cost impact per fallback.
[06:10] Tom Greer: Show me the KV cache — how do you do prefix caching for chat? We keep long histories.
[06:25] Maya Singh: Prefix/KV cache — we cache long static context and store token-level KV for attention cache so subsequent tokens short-circuit. For the clinical case we typically cache patient instruction templates and key-turns. Note: transcription may call it key-value cash or K-V cache occasionally.
[06:55] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Does caching change semantics? We're worried about stale patient notes.
[07:10] Maya Singh: Cache invalidation is per-session or TTL-based. You can tag cached entries with patient ids and force invalidation on updates. We recommend small TTLs for PII contexts.
[07:30] [08:00] Jordan Park: Switching to performance — we ran med-sized benchmarks for a similar customer: hosted median latency for short prompts ~80–120ms, dedicated with tensor-optimized kernels ~45–70ms depending on GPU and quantization. Key is sequence length and KV hit-rate.
[08:40] Tom Greer: How does quantization impact safety/regression? We can't lose hallucination controls.
[08:55] Maya Singh: We advise per-model quality evals — Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles by workload and run automatic evals on your prompt set. For safety sensitive rerank we often keep high-precision variants and route only low-risk workloads to quantized models.
[09:20] Dr. Aisha Rahman: For Anthropic-style safety layers, can we run the safety model in a separate route and chain calls? Latency would add up though.
[09:35] Liam Ortega: You can compose routes — run an initial filter on a cheap model, then call the higher-end model only when needed. The console shows end-to-end p95 for chained calls so you can reason about SLOs.
[09:55] [10:30] Jordan Park: Quick demo of the adapters repo — Maya, show the Together streaming adapter example.
[10:40] Maya Singh: (screen share code) Here's a node shim that translates Together streaming events into Redwood streams. We also provide a ruby/python example. For errors we map codes to HTTP 4xx/5xx equivalents so your consumers don't need code changes.
[11:05] Tom Greer: That sounds promising. How much work to integrate with our internal L7 proxies?
[11:20] Maya Singh: Minimal — the shim is middleware, drop it behind your proxy. We have example Nginx config and upstreams. We'll attach the sample during follow-up.
[11:40] [12:00] Sophie Lin: Back to security: where are audit logs stored and for how long? Can we push logs to our SIEM?
[12:15] Jordan Park: Yes — logs are pipelineable. For Dedicated and Private you can configure retention and forward logs to your SIEM or S3 bucket. Hosted customers can request log streaming with support plan. We'll share the audit log schema.
[12:40] Dr. Aisha Rahman: OK let's talk cost — we have about 3 billion tokens/month across vendors. Any rough idea of delta?
[12:55] Maya Singh: From past benchmarks, unit token cost can be 20–40% lower depending on batching and KV hit rates if you move to a dedicated pool with optimized kernels. We'll put numbers in the parity spreadsheet — includes quantized variant pricing and reserved capacity discounts.
[13:20] Tom Greer: Reserved capacity — what's minimum?
[13:30] Jordan Park: Depends on GPU size and commitment; typical entry for Dedicated is monthly with a 3–6 month commit for predictable throughput. We can sketch a pilot that's time-limited.
[13:45] [14:00] Maya Singh: Now Optimize quick-run — we fed a sample prompt set and the console suggests batching window 40–60ms and a KV TTL of 30s for your workload to hit cost/latency sweet spot. It also flagged two prompts that degrade under 8-bit quant.
[14:25] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Can Optimize run as a CI gate so new models don't regress?
[14:35] Liam Ortega: Yes — Optimize exposes an eval API and can be wired into CI to block rollouts on quality regressions. We also do rollouts with automatic rollback thresholds.
[15:00] [15:45] Jordan Park: Question from chat: "Do we support per-token streaming billing or by-response?"
[15:55] Maya Singh: By default we bill per-token for generation and per-embedding unit for embeddings. We show both raw token counts and normalized counts in the console. If you need enterprise accounting we can adapt to your internal schema.
[16:20] Dr. Aisha Rahman: About data residency — we require EU and US clusters separated, and some workloads must stay within on-prem.
[16:35] Jordan Park: We support region pinning and Private (on-prem) installs for regulated workloads. For hybrid flows you can route sensitive requests to Private and keep analytics in Hosted. We'll share architecture diagrams.
[17:00] [18:00] Sophie Lin: For pilot, we need to see sample SLA wording and a security addendum.
[18:15] Jordan Park: Will send pilot contract and an addendum; typical addendum covers encryption, key separation, and incident response timelines.
[18:40] Tom Greer: Let's try a short live test — we've got a small prompt set and one sample token budget. Can we spin a staging route?
[18:55] Maya Singh: Yes — spinning staging with a Dedicated-equivalent pool is about 15 min in our console. I'll provision a test route now.
[19:30] [20:00] (screen changes) Maya Singh: Route is up, endpoint posted in chat: https://staging.redwood/api/r/abcd1234 (placeholder). Send your prompt and I'll run both Redwood and your current vendor stacks and show deltas.
[20:50] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Sending prompt A1 for triage now.
[21:10] Maya Singh: Running Redwood -> median 62ms, token count normalized 78 tokens. Together gave 68ms on their edge, Anthropic rerank added 42ms. So end-to-end currently 110–120ms depending on chain.
[21:45] Tom Greer: Those numbers look good. What's the 95th?
[21:55] Maya Singh: On this small sample p95 95ms. With longer histories p95 goes up — that's where KV caching helps.
[22:20] [23:00] Jordan Park: Recap: parity shim minimal, console supports route pinning & SLOs, Optimize recommends batching + TTLs, Dedicated gives predictable latency and cost.
[23:35] Dr. Aisha Rahman: We liked the canary/fallback bit — important for clinical risk. Next steps for us: gather traffic shape and prompt families, review your parity spreadsheet, run a 48-hour perf smoke test, and review the SOC2/KMS docs.
[23:55] Jordan Park: Great. We'll follow up with the parity spreadsheet, pricing sketch, pilot contract, and SOC/KMS docs. I'll also set up the deep technical session with Tom for infra integration.
[24:20] Sophie Lin: One peripheral Q — do you support signed VPC peering or just egress rules?
[24:35] Liam Ortega: We support VPC peering for Dedicated and Private, and we have signed peering templates for legal. For hosted we do controlled egress with PrivateLink options.
[25:00] [25:45] (few seconds of background noise)
[26:10] Tom Greer: If we run pilot, can we get a temporary reserved node so we can test autoscaling at higher loads?
[26:25] Jordan Park: Yes temporary capacity reservations are common for pilots — we'll include that in the pricing sketch.
[26:45] Dr. Aisha Rahman: How do you handle model rollbacks? We need a very quick revert path.
[26:58] Maya Singh: Console rollouts are atomic per-route; you can set auto-rollback thresholds based on p95, error rate, or custom eval metrics and it will revert to previous model automatically.
[27:20] [28:00] Jordan Park: Final logistics — we aim to get the parity sheet and pricing to you by Tuesday (2026-12-29). Pilot provisioning can start as soon as you hand over prompt set and traffic profile (Tom's action).
[28:30] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Sounds good. Sophie — will you compile compliance asks?
[28:40] Sophie Lin: Yep, I'll email a prioritized list.
[28:55] Jordan Park: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and schedule the deep-dive.

Closing Recap (auto-generated):
- Parity adapter is small shim; Redwood provides examples for Together/Anthropic/OpenAI mappings.
- Console handles per-route SLOs, rollouts, cost visibility.
- Optimize suggests batching and quantization profiles but flags safety-critical prompts for higher precision.
- Security: KMS/BYOK, VPC peering, audit log streaming supported.
- Next steps: parity spreadsheet, pricing/pilot sketch, 48-hour perf smoke test, schedule infra deep-dive.

Links & artifacts mentioned: https://redwood.ai/decks/sable-migration (deck), parity-spreadsheet (will be shared), staging endpoint placeholder, SOC2 + KMS guide (follow-up).

End of transcript.
